headline: A 2018 law lets the Treasury Department mint commemorative coins honoring the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, with sales surcharges going to the Hall.
what_it_does: The Treasury Department must mint and issue up to 50,000 $5 coins, 400,000 $1 coins, and 750,000 half-dollar coins to honor the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. The coins are dome-shaped and show a basketball on the reverse side. Treasury will hold a design competition for the obverse, which must reflect the game of basketball. Every coin sale must include a set surcharge, and Treasury pays those surcharges to the Hall to fund an endowment for its operations and education programs.

who_it_affects.how: People who buy these commemorative coins pay the coin price plus the required surcharge.

who_it_affects.group: The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame
who_it_affects.how: The Hall receives surcharge money from Treasury to build an endowment for operations and educational programming.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Mint and Department of the Treasury
who_it_affects.how: Treasury must run a design competition, mint the coins in the set quantities, and pay the surcharges to the Hall.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a specific effective date; the act was enacted on December 21, 2018.
